national.title: Carney to push for closer ties at Canada-EU summit in Montreal
national.summary: The term "associate member" is reportedly off the table as officials discuss deeper economic and defence ties.
national.body:
For decades, Canada-EU summits took place without much fanfare - but that's not the case for this coming two-day meeting in Montreal.

Thursday and Friday's summit will be closely watched for details on how Canada and the European bloc deepen their ties.

Last month, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen proposed "opening the door" to Canada for what she called an "associate membership" - a status that does not currently exist.

The overture came after Prime Minister Carney addressed the European Parliament in Strasbourg, telling EU lawmakers that Canada and Europe were "stronger together" in the face of "geopolitical rupture".

Von der Leyen, speaking to reporters after landing in Montreal on Wednesday, said the two sides will "start discussing how to make Canada the first associate member of the EU".

"Our ambition is to build the closest partnership we have ever had with a non-European country," she said.

Carney and many EU member states welcome closer ties, but not all are on board with what to call this new relationship.

Some, like Germany, are questioning the "associate member" term, fearing that Canada is getting preferential treatment ahead of other nations who also want in.

national.title: DoorDash gobbles up Instacart in $17 billion deal
national.summary: DoorDash's purchase of Instacart for $65 per share will unite two of the country's largest grocery and food-delivery companies.
national.body: DoorDash said Thursday that it will buy Instacart for $17 billion, uniting one of the nation's top grocery delivery services with a major food delivery company. DoorDash, which will pay $65 per share for Instacart, said the acquisition will benefit communities by enabling more supermarkets to use Instacart's platform to run their websites. "Instacart has spent years learning to do that well for grocers, while DoorDash has built a delivery network and technology that local stores rely on every day," Tony Xu, co-founder and CEO of DoorDash, said in a statement. "Together, we could give stores of every size more of those tools and unlock the potential of grocery delivery."Consumers will benefit by having more stores to choose from, speedier delivery options and access to savings when they shop locally, DoorDash also said in announcing the acquisition. The announcement comes as more people shift away from in-person stores and toward apps to order their weekly groceries. Nearly 150 million Americans grocery shopped online as of 2025, according to Capital One. DoorDash said the companies will operate as separate entities until the merger is finalized, which is expected in late 2027 or early 2028. After the deal closes, DoorDash said it plans to maintain Instacart's brand, technology and app.â This is a breaking news story and will be developed.

national.summary: DEA Special Agent David Howell tells CBS News the agency tasked with enforcing federal drug laws has allowed millions of fentanyl pills to hit the streets.
national.body: As New Mexico officials sounded alarms this month about a growing fentanyl crisis, a veteran Drug Enforcement Administration agent has alleged the agency has contributed to the problem by allowing the deadly pills to reach the streets."For three years, I've told my DEA managers that we're allowing dangerous amounts of fentanyl to hit the street, and we're doing nothing to stop it, and they didn't listen to me," DEA Special Agent David Howell told CBS News in his first television interview.Howell, who is still an active agent, claims the agency tasked with enforcing federal drug laws has allowed millions of fentanyl pills to "walk" — a tactic in which investigators allow drug traffickers to distribute their product and then follow the trail to build bigger cases.But because fentanyl is so lethal, Howell said the tactic has done more harm than good."We at the DEA have let drugs hit the street, yes. The difference was we were told not to with fentanyl," he said. In 2023, Howell was part of a team tracking a suspect in Albuquerque from the air. Images obtained by CBS News from congressional investigators on the House Oversight Committee showed a person driving a white SUV picking up a child."We knew we weren't going to let the drugs … hit the streets or go to the house when we knew the kid was in the car," Howell said. Agents in a black truck stopped the SUV, secured the child and detained the suspect."We took his drugs. We took his gun. It was in a little compartment underneath the seat that the child was sitting on," Howell said.Howell said agents found between 6,000 and 7,000 fentanyl pills in the vehicle. But he says they faced backlash for taking the fentanyl pills off the streets."We thought the U.S. Attorney's Office [for the District of New Mexico] would be pleased," Howell said. "Instead, they brought us into their office and chastised us. They were perfectly willing to allow that fentanyl to go to the house with the kid."Howell's whistleblower complaint was first reported last June by the Associated Press and Albuquerque Journal. national.title: Ship sunk by infamous Nazi sub in 1944 found off coast of Maine
national.summary: The U-boat that landed two Nazi spies on the Maine coast sank the 400-foot steamship SS Cornwallis four days later.
national.body: A German submarine slipped through frigid New England waters and covertly dropped off two Nazi spies in Maine on Nov. 29, 1944. Their assignment was to gather intelligence in the United States at the height of World War II.Just four days later, the same U-boat spotted a merchant ship in the area and fired a torpedo that struck its cargo hold. The vessel, a 400-foot Canadian steamship called SS Cornwallis, sank in just 10 minutes. Only five of the 48 people on board survived.Now, more than 80 years later, the wreckage of the Cornwallis has been found. The ship was finally located in July nearly 400 feet below the ocean's surface, the Nomad Exploration Team announced this week.The New Hampshire-based team said it had to contend with cold water, strong currents and remote locations to reach the massive vessel. Finally, side scan sonar revealed the wreck, and later dives confirmed the vessel's identity, the team said."For the team, finding the wreck was the culmination of years of persistence," said dive team member Danny Allan. "For the families and communities connected to the ship, it brings renewed attention to a largely forgotten tragedy."The Cornwallis' final voyageLaunched in 1921, the Cornwallis was a 5,458-ton steam merchant ship built in Vancouver, British Columbia. Originally called the Canadian Transporter, the ship was later renamed Cornwallis after transferring to Canadian National Steamships. On Sept. 11, 1942, while anchored in Barbados, a German sub fired torpedoes at the Cornwallis, severely damaging the vessel. However, the ship only partially sank in shallow waters and was later repaired and put back in service.In November 1944, the ship left Barbados packed with a cargo of sugar and molasses, bound for St. John, New Brunswick. According to nautical historian Eric Wiberg, the Cornwallis was equipped with a 4-inch gun, a 12-pound gun and machine guns on the bridge. None of the weapons were ever fired.On Dec. 3, as the ship moved along the Maine coastline, it was spotted by the German submarine U-1230, commanded by Hans Hilbig. The U-boat fired a torpedo that struck near the Cornwallis' bow and the vessel plunged below the surface in less than 10 minutes.Only six of the 48 people aboard were able to reach life rafts, and one died of hypothermia. national.title: Record number of purges as Xi emphasises 'party discipline' at China political gathering
national.summary: Xi's anti-corruption campaign has become "an effort to consolidate and maintain authority", observers say.
national.body:
A record 33 members have been expelled from China's Communist Party as it concluded a major annual political gathering, which had the most empty seats ever seen.

The fifth plenum was attended by 279 Central Committee members, compared to 315 at the fourth plenum in October 2025 and 364 at the third one in July 2024.

While recent plenums focused on economic reforms or social and development issues, party discipline took centre stage at this week's gathering.

Xi Jinping has made the fight against corruption a central pillar of his rule since he took the reins in 2012, calling it the "biggest threat" to the party.

Sixteen of the 33 members expelled are from the military, according to a communique issued on Thursday, which marked the end of the four-day closed-door gathering held at a hotel in Beijing.

It's unclear what specific charges these members face beyond "serious disciplinary and legal violations". Such broad allegations have become routine under Xi's anti-corruption campaign.

It has now become "an effort to consolidate and maintain authority", says Chong Ja Ian, a non-resident scholar with Carnegie China.

"In this case, the campaign will continue and expand depending on how secure Xi feels rather than any real issue with corruption."

national.title: First map of U.S. Mason-Dixon Line going up for auction
national.summary: The first map of the Mason-Dixon Line dividing U.S. Northern free states from Southern states that had slavery decades before the Civil War is going up for auction.
national.body: It's perhaps the most consequential map in American history. And it could be yours. The hand-drawn chart of the Mason-Dixon Line that eventually divided the free from the slave states is going up for auction.Remounted on backing made of Japanese rice paper, the document will go on sale Thursday in a livestreamed event. "It's not that often that you can really get this close to something that is so historically important," said Lauren Brunk, vice president of Brunk Auctions in Asheville, North Carolina. "And it was awe-inspiring, really."Brunk estimates it could fetch anywhere from $800,000 to $1.2 million for the anonymous seller."Drawn between 1767 and 1768 by Charles Mason ... and Jeremiah Dixon ... the Mason-Dixon Line is the symbolic boundary between Northern and Southern states," Brunk says on its website. The survey by Charles Mason and Jeremiah Dixon was originally meant to settle a border dispute between the then-colonies of Maryland and Pennsylvania. But when it was used in the 1820 Missouri Compromise to establish the limits of human bondage in the still adolescent United States, it became synonymous with the fundamental divisions that exploded into Civil War four decades later. "The Mason-Dixon Line that most Americans know is this dividing line between the Northern free states and the Southern slaveholding states," Brunk said. "But the line was not drawn for that reason." A popular theory is that the term "Dixie" comes from Dixon, though the true origin is disputed. Soon after it was drawn, the linen-backed strip of paper -- 76 inches long and 6.5 inches tall -- was given to the family of attorney Benjamin Chew, who represented the descendants of Pennsylvania founder William Penn. The map remained in the family's hands until 1982, when late publisher Malcolm S. Forbes outbid the Library of Congress and bought it for $360,000, Brunk said. At the time, it was said to have been the highest price ever paid at auction for an American map. The map changed hands again in 2002. A vertical section showing the Delaware-Maryland border is housed at Princeton University. Brunk reached out to officials at the Library of Congress to see if they wanted to bid on it again. national.title: Alaska governor orders probe into Democratic campaign's alleged links to same-name candidate
national.summary: The Republican governor was responding to allegations in the New York Times that Democrats recruited a spoiler candidate, Dan Sullivan.
national.body:
The Republican governor of Alaska has ordered an investigation into an alleged "scheme" which led to two Dan Sullivans standing in the state's US Senate race.

Governor Mike Dunleavy said he was responding to a New York Times (NYT) story , external which said the team of Democratic candidate Mary Peltola worked with people who tried to recruit spoiler candidates in the Senate race.

The governor's post on X said he would investigate "whether this scheme violated Alaska's laws". He did not say which laws he had in mind.

Dan Sullivan, the incumbent Republican senator running for re-election, and allies have accused the Democrats of trying to confuse voters. Peltola's team deny any wrongdoing.

They say they did not encourage the second Dan Sullivan, a retired teacher who lives in a remote fishing village, to stand. He has denied any links with the Peltola campaign.

Although he has given few interviews, he told the NYT , external in August he was running the race in good faith as a moderate Republican, albeit that he had voted for Peltola in previous contests.

The ballot paper is set to list the two men as Dan S Sullivan, who will be described as the incumbent Republican senator, and Daniel J Sullivan Jr.

Senator Dan Sullivan told Fox News on Wednesday night that Peltola should "come clean" and described it as a scandal of the highest order.

national.title: Netanyahu's bloc leading Israel election but short of majority, partial results show
national.summary: With 93% of ballots counted, Netanyahu's Likud party and its allies are set to win 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset.
national.body:
Partial results from Israel's general election show veteran Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu marginally ahead of his rival, former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, but still short of a majority in parliament.

With 93% of ballots counted, Netanyahu's Likud party and its far-right and ultra-Orthodox Jewish allies were on track to win 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset. Eisenkot's Yashar party and three other Jewish opposition parties in his bloc were set for 48.

Both leaders have said they will try to form a governing coalition.

Arab-led parties, which are on course to win an unprecedented 19 seats, could emerge as kingmakers. But all but one of the Jewish parties have pledged not to work with them.

On Thursday, officials began counting as many as 480,000 absentee ballots from groups including soldiers, diplomats and hospital patients, who could not get to polling stations.

These votes may change the final number of seats allotted to each party under Israel's proportional representation system.

Once the results are confirmed, President Isaac Herzog will hold consultations with all the political factions and invite the leader whom he believes has the best chance of success to form a government - a process that could take weeks.

If they fail, then ultimately there would have to be another election.

national.title: Audio reveals exchanges between control centre and drivers before deadly Spain train crash
national.summary: The recordings appear to show one high-speed train was given clearance to move even though another up ahead had stalled.
national.body:
Audio recordings published in Spanish media reveal conversations between train drivers and a railway control centre in the minutes leading up to a deadly train crash that killed at least 69 people and injured dozens.

Officials are investigating the cause of the disaster, which occurred when a train travelling from Madrid to Seville barrelled into a stationary train on Wednesday morning.

Three audio recordings between the control centre in Madrid and two train drivers appear to show that one high-speed train was given clearance to move even though another some 25km (15 miles) up ahead had stalled.

Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, who travelled to the area of the crash, said authorities were working "day and night" to "get to the bottom of every last detail of this tragedy".

The release of the recordings comes as Spain begins three days of national mourning for one of the worst rail disasters in Europe's modern history.

One train, run by state-owned operator Renfe, had 397 passengers on board. Ahead of it on the same line was a train run by private operator Iryo, with 147 passengers.

A reported issue with the automatic signalling system - a computer failure - had forced all trains to halt on the affected stretch.

But later the Renfe train was ordered to proceed in "error", according to Spain's transport minister.

national.summary: More than 500 passengers were on board the trains when the crash occurred in the province of Toledo, south of Madrid.
national.body:
Two trains crashed south of the Spanish capital Madrid on Wednesday morning, on the high-speed line to Seville.

At least 69 people died in the collision, when a state-operated Renfe train went into the back of a stationary train operated by the Iryo company near the town of Urda.

The crash happened at 08:53 (07:53 GMT) between municipalities Mora and Orgaz, and about 140km (100 miles) south of Madrid, according to an account given by the Spanish government.

The privately run Iryo train appears to have been stationary on the state-run Renfe train barrelled into the back of it at high speed. Iryo said its train was "struck from behind" by a Renfe train "due to causes that are still unknown".

All train traffic on the line was stopped at stations along the route.

Renfe said services between Madrid, Ciudad Real and Andalusia were suspended.

A passenger on board one of the trains told local media there was a heavy impact about 40 minutes into the journey.

national.title: 'I live with a ghost' - inside the haunted homes attracting bargain hunters
national.summary: Properties where someone has died in tragic circumstances can have big reductions in price.
national.body:
From the moment Ryua first walked into her rental apartment in Tokyo she believed it to be haunted.

"When I visited the place for a viewing there was a man standing there, glaring at me," she says.

"Since the estate agent couldn't see him, I realised he must be a ghost."

While someone more squeamish would probably have quickly left the flat never to return, Ryua chose to go ahead and move in.

"I'm a bit of a contrarian, so I decided I wanted to become friends with this glaring male ghost," adds Ryua, who works as an aidoru, a young entertainer, and who doesn't wish to share her surname.

Four years later, and still in the same apartment, she says she continues to experience paranormal activity on a daily basis. She says she hears endless footsteps and the ghost talking.

Although Japan has increasingly marked Halloween , external in recent years, many Japanese people take ghosts seriously all year round. The country has a word, "yuurei", which means a lingering, troubled spirit.

These are the ghosts of people who died in violent or tragic circumstances - those who were murdered, killed themselves, or simply were lonely and died alone. If they died at home, then the belief is that their yuurei won't go away.

national.title: Audacious Indian jailbreak saga ends with 17 prisoners recaptured
national.summary: The jailbreak began with a fake seizure and ended 36 hours later with all the inmates back behind bars.
national.body:
A fake medical emergency, an audacious jailbreak and a 36-hour search operation that ended with 17 prisoners being recaptured.

Those are the highlights of a story from India's Tamil Nadu state that has captured headlines across the country.

It began on Monday night after 17 men escaped from a prison in Theni district in the southern state after overpowering guards, and ended almost two days later with police catching them in batches.

The incident has drawn attention to overcrowding in Indian prisons. Police say the Theni prison was housing 334 inmates against a capacity of 200, leaving authorities unable to maintain control once chaos broke out.

The state police said it has suspended nine staff at the prison for alleged negligence in connection with the incident.

All the men who escaped were undertrials - inmates on trial or awaiting one - and 18 of them were in one cell at the prison in Thekkampatti in Theni.

On Monday night at 2230 local time (17:00 GMT), one of the prisoners acted like he was going through a seizure. The other cellmates shouted for help and a jail official responded. He was soon overpowered by the prisoners, police said.

The prisoners then got out of the cell, reportedly attacked two other jail guards and took away keys which they used to open the main gate and flee. While 17 escaped, one returned to the prison immediately.

national.title: How could Israel break election deadlock? Here are four scenarios
national.summary: With more than 90% of votes counted, all signs point to an impasse. The most likely outcome may be new elections.
national.body:
With more than 90% of votes counted after Tuesday's election, neither the incumbent Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition, nor the bloc of his key challenger Gadi Eisenkot look set to win a majority.

In order to a form a government, it looks likely one of the leading parties would have to break their campaign promises - meaning the most probable outcome may well be new elections.

Could Netanyahu persuade Eisenkot to join him in a national unity government?

Eisenkot would have to abandon his key platform to do so. He's framed himself as the only alternative to Netanyahu, and built his campaign on ousting him from power.

On election night, he took to the stage at his campaign HQ and called on Netanyahu to "announce his retirement from political life today," telling the crowd that Israelis are fed up with Netanyahu's "culture of lies", "division and incitement".

But that was before one of the main exit polls - which had initially projected a lead for Eisenkot's bloc - was revised, and he was overtaken by Netanyahu.

Netanyahu could try to persuade Eisenkot's Yashar Party to join his Likud Party in a unity government by ditching the far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties he is currently in coalition with. But last night at Likud HQ he thanked his "loyal partners" and called for a "strong right-wing government" - remarks some have interpreted as meaning he intends to preserve his alliance with them.

One thing that could make a unity government more likely is a renewed conflict with Iran, which could place serious pressure on party leaders to put aside their political differences and work together. In the days prior to the election, Israeli and US media reported that Netanyahu was pushing for fresh strikes on the country, and had pressed Donald Trump to approve US involvement.

Whether or not they live in a competitive congressional district, voters in many states will be deciding on statewide ballot measures with a chance to make law themselves.

There are 145 statewide ballot measures on the November ballot, according to Ballotpedia, which tracks elections.

In some cases the questions were put on the ballot with petition drives by citizens frustrated with the actions - or lack of action - by their state lawmakers. In many cases, legislatures go to the voters with amendments to their state constitution.

There are common themes across the country: many of the most high profile referenda are on abortion, LGBTQ+ rights, taxes, and voting.

Four states have abortion on the ballot. That comes after a flurry of ballot measures on the issue since federal protections for the procedure from Roe v. Wade were overturned by the Dobbs decision in 2022.

Elections Some states will ask voters to make it harder to pass constitutional amendments Just two years ago, Missouri voters nullified what had been one of the strictest abortion bans in the country. But the Republican-led legislature has put the question back on the ballot. And lawmakers crafted a single question that includes both a near-total ban on abortion and prohibitions on gender-affirming medical treatments for minors.

Abortion is legal in Nevada and Virginia but voters in both states will have a chance to put those rights in the state constitution. That would make it harder for future legislatures to ban abortion.

national.title: These are the House races to watch in the 2026 midterm election on Nov. 3
national.summary: An NPR analysis finds 70 House districts where Democrats and Republicans are each investing more than six figures in advertising during the final few days of the election, including in deep red areas.
national.body:
In the final week of the 2026 midterm election, ad spending data suggests the core battle is less about stopping a Democratic wave in the House, and more about figuring out how high it crests.

An NPR analysis finds the final competitive House landscape is expansive, including 70 districts where both parties are investing at least six figures per district into their final days of messaging.

That includes more than $10 million each in toss up districts in Michigan, North Carolina, New York and Florida; seven figure ad buys in deep-red communities across Tennessee, Oklahoma and Arkansas and last-minute resources to districts where gerrymandering by Republicans could backfire.

Elections In Arkansas, Democrats see an opening at the edge of the competitive midterms map In a midterm environment that disfavors the party in power, Republicans' narrow 218-214 seat advantage in the House appears all but certain to give way to Democratic control. The latest ratings from the Cook Political Report finds Democrats favored in 220 seats, 17 listed as "toss-ups" and another 30 that are potentially competitive but lean toward the GOP.

Most of the seats that saw narrow margins in the 2024 presidential election cycle have shifted the way of the Democrats, especially in the 10 districts that voted for one party's presidential candidate and the other party's House nominee.

That includes seats held by Democratic Reps. Adam Gray (CA-13), Nellie Pou (NJ-09) and Marie Gluesenkamp-Perez (WA-03) and retiring Republican Rep. Don Bacon (NE-02).

All four of those districts have seen Republicans slash ad reservations in recent weeks, according to AdImpact data.

The latest NPR/PBS News/Marist poll finds Democrats have a 10-point advantage among registered voters and 8 points with likely voters on the generic congressional ballot. That means a far broader number of seats are competitive on paper, before accounting for candidate quality or outside spending.

national.title: Tariffs, diesel and computer chips are driving up costs for automakers
national.summary: American auto companies say they are paying more for key components like computer chips, steel and copper — plus the fuel needed to transport their products.
national.body:
American automakers are reporting their third quarter earnings, and they're saying revenues are up, but they're also facing some serious headwinds.

Or as Mike Wall, an analyst at the automotive data company Mobility Global, put it: If this year was a book about the auto industry, "It would be a mix of suspense and thrills and maybe a little bit of comedy and a little bit of horror."

For the thrills: Auto companies are doing well when it comes to selling big cars and light-duty trucks. General Motors reported its sales of light-duty trucks rose 9% in the past year . Ford's F-Series trucks continue to be a company bestseller . Stellantis' pickup sales in the U.S. rose 34% .

And revenues overall are up: General Motors reported its revenue was up 2.9% in the past year; for Ford it was a 2% rise and Stellantis was up 1% .

Affordability How long does it take to save up for a starter home? Twice as long as it did in 2019 What It Takes What's gone up even faster than gas or rent? The cost of caregiving To analysts, all of this signals that consumers are still buying vehicles — despite concerns about affordability. The average new vehicle transaction price was just over $50,000 in September, close to a record high, according to the Kelley Blue Book . Broadly speaking, customers are paying more for high-end trims and for bigger vehicles, which tend to be more profitable for the auto companies.

"Customers have been resilient amid higher fuel prices, interest rates and inflation," said Sherry Ann House, Ford's chief financial officer, on a call with investors.

But now for the suspense: The Detroit Three automakers are also cautioning investors that it's getting more expensive to make cars. Key materials like steel, copper and computer chips have all gotten pricier.

"Should we see prices at this level, it makes that more challenging heading into next year," Paul Jacobson, the chief financial officer of General Motors, said on the company's earnings call.

national.title: Ahead of midterms, Missourians defend transgender healthcare
national.summary: The campaign to defend access to transgender healthcare for young people in Missouri is taking an unhurried approach to talking with voters about the proposed ban.
national.body:
A campaign to defend transgender healthcare for young people in Missouri is taking an unhurried approach by talking with voters about the latest attempt to permanently ban gender-affirming care for minors in the state.

CREVE COEUR, Mo. — Reneé Luckfield tries not to knock like a cop.

In fact, the 29-year-old spends a lot of time thinking about how to make strangers comfortable when she shows up at their door to talk about transgender healthcare. A syncopated "tap — tap-tap-tap" sounds friendly even when she knocks loudly. In each encounter, she masks her own unease.

"Honestly, it's not something that I'm entirely comfortable with," Luckfield, a transgender woman, said while walking door to door in this affluent St. Louis suburb. "And it's not fair that we have to do this work."

Only on NPR New maps reveal massive gaps in access to affordable birth control across the U.S Transgender issues have become a major theme in this year's midterm elections, especially in Missouri, where voters are weighing a proposed constitutional amendment to bar minors from gender-transition surgery, cross-sex hormone therapy and puberty blockers. The potential ban is part of a proposed amendment to reinstate a near-total ban on abortion in the state.

Voters in four other states will also decide on transgender issues this year: a proposed ban on transgender health care for minors in Colorado, and proposed restrictions on transgender athletes in youth sports in Arizona, Colorado, Nebraska and Washington.

Luckfield is part of an effort by the LGBTQ+ advocacy organization PROMO Missouri to defeat the Missouri measure by knocking on 100,000 doors across five of the state's largest metro areas before the election — an ambitious target the group is trying to reach with a mixture of full-time canvassers like Luckfield, the St. Louis lead, and volunteers who show up on weekends. About one out of every 10 knocks turns into a conversation, and they're aiming to have 10,000 conversations before Election Day. The group celebrated reaching 6,000 in early October, but the process is slow going, intentionally, as canvassers aim for open-ended, "transformative" conversations with potential voters.

The technique, "deep canvassing," has a history of changing people's perspectives on difficult political topics, including a 2012 campaign that overturned a gay marriage ban in Maine and a 2021 campaign for police reform in Minnesota that, while defeated, triggered new debate. Now, organizers in Missouri hope it can help stave off the latest effort in the state to permanently ban gender-affirming care for minors.

national.summary: Opposition to the rapid emergence of data centers in states such as Ohio and Arizona has ginned up activism and unified voters. A range of public health issues have played into the resistance.
national.body: Page, Arizona — Doug Herrera still lives in the house his father built, though his dad died some time ago from cancer. Herrera wonders if that illness could have been linked to pollutants from nearby uranium mining. Now, he worries that a possible new neighbor — a proposed $10 billion mega data center — could imperil his health."I'm a patriot, but I'm highly against the data center," Herrera, 64, said from his front porch near a yard sign that reads "No Data Centers.""There is light pollution, sound pollution. The temperature is going to rise," he said.Page is a gateway to iconic Southwestern landscapes of arid desert studded with Joshua trees and towering red-rock formations. While the City Council approved the sale of land for a data center, the developer needs zoning and other approvals. Residents concerned about possible health effects have signed petitions and mobilized to oppose construction.The boom in data centers is dividing communities such as Page and turning future construction into a flash point in the midterm elections. The leading candidates in the close race for Arizona's 1st Congressional District are at odds over any new centers there, and the state's attorney general has called for a pause on new approvals and building.Emerging research into data centers' possible health effects is adding grist to the various state fights, giving ammunition to Democrats and some Republicans who've broken party ranks to oppose the sprawling complexes.It has also put some incumbent politicians who have supported data center expansion in unexpectedly vulnerable positions in reliably red states like Ohio and Texas, where the megabuildings now operate by the hundreds."Two years ago, a lot of these data centers went up and there was not an organized, watchful opposition," said Lee Hannah, a political science professor at Wright State University in Dayton, Ohio."That opposition has come up in a grassroots way so quickly that decisions made a year ago by local officials or state governments to get behind a data center are suddenly career-ending."The hyperscale centers house infrastructure to power AI, with servers that sprawl over tens of thousands of square feet or more. national.title: Ethiopia acquires Russian fighter jets and air defence systems amid war in Tigray
national.summary: The acquisition of the warplanes comes amid ongoing fighting in northern Tigray region that started last month.
national.body:
Ethiopia has received 12 Su-35 fighter jets from Russia, as fighting intensified in the northern Tigray region neighbouring Eritrea.

Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed, who is attending the Russia-Africa summit in Moscow, described the acquisition as a "milestone" that would boost Ethiopia's defence capacity.

He said Ethiopia and Russia agreed on the deal several years ago and the warplanes had come ahead of schedule. He also said that Ethiopia had plans to acquire four S-400 air defence systems from Moscow.

The Ethiopian leader said the military hardware was essential to protect the country from external threats.

Abiy, who described Russian President Vladimir Putin, "as a close friend of Ethiopia", said Ethiopia had now become the first country in sub‑Saharan Africa to own this kind of "advanced combat technology."

"If we fail to build this capability, surviving as a country in our region will become difficult. Countries with sufficient preparation are not easily defied," he said.

Russia and Ethiopia have signed several military agreements in recent years, including a deal in 2021 to train and improve technology for the military.

Abiy explained that Ethiopia signed an agreement with Russia several years ago to procure the Su‑35 jets and S‑400 systems, citing global air force trends and security threats facing the country.

national.title: Hello Kitty maker cuts ties with Japanese spy drama after China backlash
national.summary: Sanrio has apologised after its merchandise line with Japanese TV series Vivant drew criticism.
national.body:
Sanrio, the company behind Hello Kitty, has apologised and ended its merchandise partnership with a controversial Japanese TV show after drawing backlash in China.

Vivant, a popular spy thriller, has been widely slammed in Chinese state media and by Chinese social media users for its depiction of Chinese agents using brutal torture tactics on a Japanese operative.

The criticism has extended to the internationally beloved Hello Kitty and her friends, including My Melody and Cinnamoroll, who were featured in merchandise dressed as characters from the show.

Sanrio said it terminated its collaboration with Vivant after determining that it "contained elements inconsistent with Sanrio's core values".

"Since its inception, Sanrio has consistently used its characters to convey values such as care and connection, and remains committed to its corporate philosophy of fostering harmony among all people," Sanrio said in the statement late on Wednesday.

"We take the feedback we have received regarding this incident very seriously. Moving forward, we will strengthen our review processes for all future collaborative projects."

China-Japan ties have plunged to their lowest point in years, since Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's comments on Taiwan last November sparked a diplomatic firestorm.

Responding to a question in parliament, Takaichi suggested that Japan would activate its self-defence force if China attacked Taiwan .

national.body:
El Salvador has deployed more than 2,000 soldiers to Haiti as part of a mission to retrieve four nationals who went missing in the Caribbean country almost two weeks ago.

The "robust deployment" was communicated by El Salvador President Nayib Bukele to the Prime Minister of Haiti Alix Didier Fils-Aime earlier this week, the foreign ministry of El Salvador said in a statement on Wednesday.

Bukele said the soldiers would also assist ongoing "security efforts against gangs in Haiti", the statement continued.

Tensions between the two central American countries have escalated over the disappearance of the four air force technicians working as part of a UN-backed anti-gang organisation in Haiti.

The four soldiers with the Gang Suppression Force (GSF) were travelling back to their base in an armoured vehicle when they were ambushed in an area of the Caribbean island nation controlled by armed groups called Croix-des-Bouquets.

The Salvadoran foreign ministry said the "large-scale operation" was "supported by various countries and international organisations".

Earlier this week, Haiti handed four bodies over to special forces claiming they belonged to those of the missing servicemen, but Bukele said they did not match.

He said one of the corpses was a child's and another was wearing a different country's military uniform.

national.title: Spain reckons with 2nd deadly train crash of the year ahead of national election
national.summary: Spain's second high-speed rail disaster this year, a crash in which one train struck another from behind, killing 68 people, has raised fresh concerns about the safety of the country's rail network.
national.body:
Emergency services work at the scene of a collision between two trains in Urda, Spain, on Wednesday, Oct. 28, 2026. Manu Fernandez/AP hide caption

URDA, Spain — Spain's second high-speed rail disaster this year, a crash in which one train struck another from behind, killing 68 people, has raised fresh concerns about the safety of the country's rail network.

Spain's network of high-speed rail has been considered one of the nation's crowning achievements. It ranks second to China in track mileage in the world. Until this year, it had not endured a deadly crash since coming into service over three decades ago.

The collision Wednesday that turned a sleepy stretch of rail lined by olive groves into a scene of carnage came just four weeks before the country votes in a national election.

Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez visited the crash site in the central province of Toledo after regional authorities confirmed that more than 60 people had died and dozens more were being treated at hospitals.

Only in January, 46 people had died when one train jumped the track and slammed into the side of another going the opposite way in southern Spain.

The graphic above shows the placement of derailed train cars from both trains after the crash and the events leading to the crash. Phil Holm/AP hide caption

Sánchez pledged an investigation into the latest collision and improvements to prevent another tragedy like the two that have shaken trust in a rail system that carried 45 million travelers last year, including millions of tourists.

local.body:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. (AP) -- The small-ball Milwaukee Brewers playing in the smallest market in the majors are World Series champions for the first time.

Hey, Milwaukee: grab a brat, raise a beer and prepare for that parade.

Young ace Jacob Misiorowski threw 5 2/3 scoreless innings, rookie Cooper Pratt had two more hits and two RBIs, and the Brewers beat the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 in Game 5 on Wednesday night to set off a long-awaited celebration among thousands of Brewers fans in attendance at Tropicana Field.

“It’s the best feeling ever. All of our fans are here. I know the city’s waited a long, long time for this,” Milwaukee captain Christian Yelich said. “We’re so happy to bring it home to them. I can’t wait to get back there and celebrate.”

World Series MVP William Contreras hit an RBI double and Misiorowski allowed just two hits before leaving the game because of a right calf cramp. He got a standing ovation from the Brew-Crew fans, who took over the section behind Milwaukee’s dugout for the last three games.

The 22-year-old Pratt set a Series rookie record with six straight hits before a sacrifice fly in the sixth. Jackson Chourio set a five-game Series record with 11 hits.

“This is one of the greatest moments of my life. Oh my gosh. It doesn’t even feel real,” said Pratt, who made his major league debut in June. “This is surreal. It only took four months!”

The championship comes in the 58th season for a franchise that began as the Seattle Pilots in 1969 and moved to Milwaukee the following year. The Brewers’ only previous trip to the World Series in 1982 ended in heartbreak when they blew a 3-1 lead in the sixth inning of Game 7 and lost 6-3 to the St. Louis Cardinals.

local.title: Uprising in France worth U.S. attention
local.summary: For many of us the news stories about the riots that have broken out in French cities are just another story on news channels overwhelmed by stories about Iran, the midterm elections and the price of gasoline. I was like that myself, only wondering why French youth were so upset with their schools.
local.body:
For many of us the news stories about the riots that have broken out in French cities are just another story on news channels overwhelmed by stories about Iran, the midterm elections and the price of gasoline. I was like that myself, only wondering why French youth were so upset with their schools. But as the violence and size of the demonstrations increased with the presence of far left and Islamist groups I began to pay more attention, and I didn't like what I saw.

As I write this not only are Paris, Marseille and other cities in France again experiencing far left and Islamist led demonstrations, but so are cities in Italy including Milan and Rome. Demonstrations are also taking place in Madrid, Lisbon, Athens, Dublin and in cities in Albania, Serbia and Belgium that are mostly led by student groups protesting a variety of local issues like housing shortages, and government corruption. But even in most of those cases leftist and Islamist groups are at work on the fringes.

The riots in France began as high school and university student demonstrations protesting severe underfunding, dilapidated facilities, overcrowded classrooms, and teacher shortages in French public schools. One factor stands out for what precipitated these protests over the shortcomings in the French education system is that spending on France's bloated welfare state for social welfare programs, pensions and healthcare accounts for 59% of its annual budget, the largest of any nation on Earth, while only 10% is spent on education.

To pay for this system of social welfare, France has among the highest tax rates in the western world. Employer social security contributions average 45% of gross salary, while employee contributions vary from 22% to 25%. The tax on consumer goods is 20%. These taxes are a burden on taxpayers but in France over 50% of households pay no tax so that while benefiting from the system they have no hand in the game. By comparison in socialist Denmark everyone pays some tax.

France's financial woes have been further strained by an influx of illegal immigrants, and asylum seekers primarily from Sub-Saharan Central and West Africa, and the Horn of Africa. Those granted Asylum seeker status receive an allowance with a housing supplement if they cannot be housed in a reception center, have immediate comprehensive access to the French health insurance system and even receive discounts on public transportation. Undocumented aliens receive only medical aid, emergency care, and their children can attend French public schools but even those things cost the French government.

Through exploration and hands-on learning, children ages 5-10 can join Audubon Community Nature Center's (ACNC) new Nature Connections. This monthly program is offered with homeschooled students and families in mind, though others are welcome.

Beginning Wednesday, from 1 to 2 p.m. on the first Wednesdays of the month Audubon invites 5-10-year-olds to experience a hands-on and exploratory-based approach to learn about the wonders of the natural world.

ACNC Nature Educator Taylor Spontaneo is leading Nature Connections. As she describes, "Audubon is hoping to provide homeschooled children with the experience of connecting with one another as well as a guided hands-on exploration of the natural world. By letting nature be the teacher, children are encouraged to be curious and adventurous in their own way."

Each month will feature a different theme. November's theme is "Hiking Tips and Tricks." Children will learn how to use a map while navigating trails, practice identifying poison ivy vines, and discover many other skills that make a great hiker and explorer.

Children should be dressed to be indoors and outdoors, as the program will take place in both settings. Parents and guardians may drop children off, or adults are welcome to stay.

Participation is $9 for children ages 5-10, $6.75 for Nature Center members. Reservations are appreciated by calling (716) 569-2345 or going to AudubonCNC.org/hiking-tips-and-tricks. Walk-ins are welcome.

Audubon Community Nature Center is located at 1600 Riverside Road, one-quarter mile east of Route 62 between Jamestown, N.Y., and Warren, Pa. You can visit the nearly 600-acre nature preserve, check in on the live birds of prey, enjoy the Nature Play Area, and hike six miles of trails dawn until dusk daily for free.

The three-story Nature Center building houses interactive displays, live animals, the indoor Nature Play Area, the Ralph Simpson Bird Collection, and the Blue Heron Gift Shop. Visitors are welcome Mondays through Saturdays, 10 a.m.-4:30 p.m., and Sundays, 1-4:30 p.m. Nature Center members and SNAP/EBT and Arts Access cardholders have free building admission daily. Building admission is also free Sundays for non-Nature Center members.

local.summary: Gov. Kathy Hochul has signed three bills into law as Domestic Violence Awareness Month winds down. Hochul on Tuesday signed A.10960A/S.9671, which requires local Boards of Election to notify survivors at least six months in advance of their protection expiring. Such notice will remind survivors of t
local.body:
Gov. Kathy Hochul has signed three bills into law as Domestic Violence Awareness Month winds down.

Hochul on Tuesday signed A.10960A/S.9671, which requires local Boards of Election to notify survivors at least six months in advance of their protection expiring. Such notice will remind survivors of the date their protection will end and the process for filing a new request to ensure the continued confidentiality of their records.

The legislation was sponsored by Assemblywoman Linda Rosenthal, D-Manhattan, and Sen. Michelle Hinchey, D-Kingston.

"Stalking, harassment and the many other abusive tactics used by perpetrators of domestic violence often continue long after a survivor has left the situation," Rosenthal said. "The signing of this legislation will ensure that a survivor's address information can be kept private by the Board of Elections for as long as necessary, ensuring confidentiality and protecting their safety."

Under current law, domestic violence survivors can file a request with their local Board of Elections to keep their voter registration record, including their address, confidential. Any survivor at risk of physical or emotional harm to themselves or their family may apply for the four-year protection, but there is no requirement that survivors be warned before that protection expires, leaving their information vulnerable once again if they do not renew it. .

"Survivors may spend years rebuilding their lives after escaping an abusive situation," Rosenthal said. "With so much going on, it can be easy to forget to renew this crucial protection, underscoring the importance of receiving advance notice from the Board of Elections. With a simple notice, survivors will be empowered to renew these protections, shielding their addresses from those who wish to do harm."

The legislation was approved unanimously in the state Assembly and Senate.

"We must use every tool possible to ensure that survivors of domestic violence remain safe and can feel secure in their lives," Hinchey said. "Requiring the state Board of Elections to notify survivors before their confidential voter registration status expires will help prevent a lapse in this critical layer of protection. I'm proud to sponsor this legislation, and I thank Assemblymember Linda Rosenthal for her partnership in getting this done and Governor Hochul for signing it into law so that we can strengthen an important safeguard for New Yorkers."

Deborah was born in Buffalo, NY on December 9, 1948 the daughter of LeRoy and Helen (Cocoran) Goodley.

After graduating high school Deb went onto nursing school, her career as a Registered Nurse started in 1969 and spanned 35 years . She worked at the former Tri-County Hospital, Gowanda, the former Lakeshore Hospital in Irving, she retired from the former Gowanda Psychiatric Center.

Deb was a devoted mom, she loved her family, followed her faith and treasured friendships throughout her life.

Survivors include her children ; Joseph (Charity) Sweda of Gowanda, Tara (Miguel) Sanchez of Gowanda. Grandchildren; Jace , Samuel and Hunter. She shared her life with John Fisher for 20 years, John and his children Annie, Scott and Kellye and their families also survive as does her brother, Robert (Genevieve) Goodley.

HAMBURG -- After two matchups in the regular season, splitting wins in Chautauqua-Cattaraugus Athletic Association Division III, the North Collins and Maple Grove boys soccer teams were well prepared for each other in the Section VI Class D final Wednesday night at Hamburg High School.

Tied through the first 68 minutes, the game looked like it would be heading to overtime with the contest scoreless. Then in the 69th minute, North Collins sent a cross through the box and contact going after the ball saw the Eagles awarded a penalty kick.

North Collins leading scorer Neven Sheehy made no mistake from the mark and fired home the only goal of the contest to secure the Class D title.

"It's nice to get back here," North Collins head coach Jay Walters said about winning the sectional title. "Maple Grove is a great team, they came at us with such speed. We played them twice this year and split. We played them on turf, we played them on grass. They were fast, they were physically aggressive tonight. It was a really nice contest to be a part of."

Maple Grove did not ruminate on the disappointment of the penalty call and instead began pressing as hard as it had all night for a goal.

"After a four-year break, coming back I am so proud that it's these boys," Maple Grove head coach Cara Abbey stated. "I'm so proud of them, I'm thankful for them. They know how to fight, they know how to go to war with each other and there is no better group of guys to win with or lose with."

local.body:
I've been a Milky Way girl since I was five.With Halloween just around the corner, I have a mini-excuse for having my forbidden goodies in the house. The other 51 weeks a year, I can't risk even bringing them onto the property - the temptation is too strong,

In my hometown, a little mom-and-pop store - Murphy's - was directly across the street from my school. Not many days went by that I didn't stop in for my nickel Milky Way "fix." Oh yes, there was the rare Sugar Daddy or handful of Double Bubble, but mostly I stuck to the old tried and true. In later years I learned to eat Milky Ways frozen. They lasted longer that way, but I'm really amazed I still have my teeth.

I don't think I've ever bought Halloween candy without Milky Ways in the mix. These days, I'll have to admit that Butterfingers are running a close second with an occasional side trip to Heath Bars. I suppose if I had to, I could eat a Mounds bar, but like most kids who at one time or another overindulge in a candy, mine was Mounds and I got sick on them in third grade. At the time, I liked them almost as much as Milky Ways and one day I decided that my latest book from the library would be more fun to read with a stash of Mounds bars. I bought five - an entire quarter's worth - ate them all, and naturally got sick as a dog. I don't think my mother knew why but maybe the coconut breath gave me away. I steered clear of Mounds bars - and Almond Joy as well - for the next fifty or sixty years. Tom, my late husband, got so sick on candy corn when he was a kid that he couldn't even look at the "little orange teeth" as he called them.

When I started thinking about candy for this article, I was surprised how broad and eclectic my tastes are now ... from the soft New Zealand licorice that Santa brings, to maple sugar candy, to the peach sours at Peterson's Candy in Busti. I'm amazed at how much I love candy yet have to work so hard at staying away from all of it. It doesn't seem right. If God didn't want us to have candy he wouldn't have created chocolate, right? And I think it must have been one of his Celtic saints who invented butterscotch.

I like all those chewy, sugar-coated candies like spearmint leaves and spicy gumdrops, although for some reason I like them all better when they are left out and a little stale - the chew lasts longer.

"Some candy, little girl?" If I had run into that man our mothers all warned us about, I'd have been in deep trouble.

Krakowiak knows her girls well, and she saw an opportunity to not only claim the first set, but to also springboard forward into the sets that followed. All the 'Billies needed to do was be aggressive.

Fredonia scored five of the next six points to claim the first set, then throttled Salamanca in the set that followed, 25-3. The 'Billies finished off a three-set sweep of the visiting Warriors, 25-21, 25-3, and 25-15 in a Section VI Class B2 quarterfinal playoff game on Wednesday at Fredonia High School.

"Our coach really emphasized being aggressive and dominating (Salamanca). We have three 'Ds' -- dominate, devastate and destroy -- that we like to say before every match," said Fredonia senior Londyn Wilmot. "That definitely helped us get ready."

Salamanca (9-8, 10-seed) came out strong with the game's first three points. Ten points in, it was split evenly 5-5.

"Salamanca came in and fought hard. They did a great job," Krakowiak said. "They represented well."

local.title: Transgender woman says ICE tackled her at Rochester airport, held her in men's detention facility
local.summary: A transgender woman from Singapore says ICE agents arrested her at Rochester's airport and held her at an all-men's detention center in Batavia.
local.body:
A transgender woman claims she was unlawfully arrested by ICE agents this week after her flight home landed at the Rochester airport.

The agents shouted her name – Clara Tan – to confirm her identity before taking her into custody, she said. She then was taken to the detention facility in Batavia that only houses men but released hours later after a physical examination confirmed she did not have male genitalia.

"I’ve just had one of the worst 18- hour periods of my life," Tan wrote of the incident on Facebook . "I think it’s an important story to share."

Tan, 33, says four men who identified themselves as Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents approached her around 12:30 a.m. Tuesday as she left the Frederick Douglass Greater Rochester International Airport. She asked if they had a warrant, she said, then attempted to use her phone. That is when she alleges the men tackled and handcuffed her, injuring her left foot.

"I felt pain like you never felt before," she said, "and the next thing I knew, I was on the ground. And I'm thinking, all right, here we go."

ICE did not immediately respond to an email seeking comment.

Tan is originally from Singapore, and came to the United States in 2019 to attend the American Musical and Dramatic Academy in New York. She filed a petition for asylum in 2019, and had a work permit .

She was returning from California, having traveled there for a concert that got cancelled because the Japanese performers could not obtain visas.

local.summary: A 31-year-old Buffalo man is facing multiple felony charges after authorities say he held his pregnant girlfriend against her will for three days and repeatedly assaulted her before she lost her unborn baby.
local.body: A 31-year-old Buffalo man is facing multiple felony charges after authorities say he held his pregnant girlfriend against her will for three days and repeatedly assaulted her before she lost her unborn baby.Christopher Miranda was arraigned Wednesday morning in Buffalo City Court on felony counts of kidnapping, assault and unlawful imprisonment. He is being held at the Erie County Holding Center.According to court documents, Miranda allegedly confined his girlfriend to a room starting on Friday, blocking the door and refusing to allow her to eat.Investigators allege Miranda repeatedly beat the woman and attempted to strangle her multiple times.Early Tuesday morning, police said Miranda allegedly dragged the woman by her hair down 10 steps, then left her outside.The woman, whom 7 News is not identifying to protect her privacy, began bleeding and was taken by ambulance to the hospital. Her unborn baby did not survive.Investigators said the woman was approximately 25 weeks pregnant. Miranda has not been charged directly in connection with the death of the unborn child. local.title: Flu season off to unusually early start in New York
local.summary: Flu season is off to an early start in New York, with thousands of cases already reported statewide before the calendar even turns to November.
local.body: Flu season is off to an early start in New York, with thousands of cases already reported statewide before the calendar even turns to November.The New York State Department of Health declared influenza prevalent earlier this week, signaling the start of flu season.According to the state's Seasonal Respiratory Virus Dashboard, more than 3,500 flu cases and more than 230 hospitalizations were reported statewide for the week ending October 17.WATCH: Flu season off to unusually early start in New YorkAt Niagara Falls Memorial Medical Center, Branden Simone, the hospital’s director of infection prevention, said the hospital is seeing flu activity earlier than usual.“We don't see it this early ever,” Simone said. “When the Commissioner of Health declared it prevalent earlier this week, that's 53 days earlier than last year, and about 43 days earlier than average when we get the amount of cases to deem it prevalent.”Simone said the latest numbers are well ahead of the normal timeline.“We’re seeing now, in the latest data on the dashboard, 3,500 cases already in October,” Simone said. “We typically don't see that many cases until mid-November.”Niagara Falls Memorial has already seen 15 flu cases, according to Simone, well above what the hospital typically sees at this point in the season.He said the hospital is prepared but expects those numbers to quickly grow.Simone said there are several theories about what could be driving the early flu activity, including weather patterns. He also pointed to the timing of vaccinations, saying the virus is circulating before public health officials have had as much time as usual to get the vaccine out to large portions of the population, potentially leaving vulnerable people exposed earlier in the season.As flu activity increases, Simone recommends people wash their hands frequently and stay home if they are experiencing symptoms.But he said one of the most important steps people can take right now is getting vaccinated.“Get the vaccine,” Simone said. “You can get it here locally at any pharmacy. Typically there are no charges for anybody, and you can get them through your primary care, you can get them here at the hospital, anywhere you can get that vaccine.”

entertainment.title: Yungblud Exhibition Featuring Previously Unseen ‘Idols’ Photos to Open in London
entertainment.summary: The exhibition is free to attend and will mark the collection’s exclusive U.K. showcase.
entertainment.body: Yungblud is inviting fans behind the scenes of his blockbuster Idols era with a new exhibition in London, featuring previously unseen images captured by his photographer and creative director, Tom Pallant. Organized by Behind The Gallery, Yungblud: Idols will open on Nov. 20 at Union Pacific, located at the gallery’s 17 Goulston Street venue. The exhibition is free to attend and marks the collection’s exclusive U.K. showcase following its world debut in Sydney earlier this year. Pallant has worked with Yungblud since 2019, and his images have documented the British rock singer’s rise through multiple international tours and major festival appearances including Glastonbury and Coachella. The new exhibition captures the creative process of Idols , Yungblud’s latest studio album, which was released last summer and hit the summit of the Official U.K. Albums Chart , marking the 29-year-old’s fourth No. 1 record in his home nation. The exhibition will also feature two special events across its opening weekend. An album playback is scheduled for Nov. 20, followed by an Q&A with Pallant the next day. Further details about the events will be announced in due course. Visitors will also have the opportunity to purchase photographs from the collection. Each print will be hand signed by Pallant and produced on fine-art paper. In a statement, Pallant said: “Being able to bring this show to London and share the Idols world at home is going to be super special. As we close the chapter on Idols , this feels like the right moment to bring together a collection of our favourite work, including a lot of images that both we and others might have missed along the way. “This exhibition builds on the foundation we made in Sydney. I’ve always been drawn to the moments that happen around a performance as much as the performance itself, the exhaustion, the chaos, the feeling of putting everything you have into something. I’m hoping people are able to view Idols as a whole project and see the journey we all went on.” Stephen Dallimore, creative director of Behind The Gallery, added: “Tom Pallant’s photography uniquely captures the raw emotional energy of Yungblud, an artist who has taken the world by storm, and it feels only right that U.K. fans now get to be part of that story. It’s very rare that one photographer can tell an artist’s world like Tom can with Yungblud. Over the course of the exhibition, we’ll celebrate with fans these powerful images through photography, music and storytelling.” Pallant has previously released a photography book titled All My Friends Have Deserted Me , which chronicled Yungblud’s journey through to his sold-out show at London’s Alexandra Palace in 2021. He has also won three Abbey Road Music Photography Awards over the years. entertainment.title: U2 to Play Rare, Intimate London Show for BBC Music in November
entertainment.summary: The rare gig for a select group of fans will include the live debut of tracks from the band's upcoming Carnaval de Luz album.
entertainment.body:
While they typically fill stadiums around the world, U2 will go small next week when they play an exclusive, intimate show for BBC Music. The Nov. 3 performance at an as-yet-unannounced central London venue will feature a select group of fans who will see the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame band play classics from their catalog as well as new songs from their upcoming Carnaval de Luz LP.

The show will be broadcast on BBC Two in late November as part of a night of programming dedicated to the band, with the show also available on the BBC iPlayer and BBC Sounds after the broadcast.

In addition, the group will be holding Carnaval De Luz global listening parties in which fans can get a first chance to hear the band’s 16th studio album, due out on Nov. 15, at participating record stores around the world from Nov. 12-15. The events will feature giveaways and prizes and take place at multiple locations in Arizona, California, Colorado, Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, Missouri, Nevada, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Texas, Washington and Wisconsin.

There will also be listening events at stores across the U.K. and in Austria, Belgium, Germany, Ireland, Italy, Mexico, the Netherlands, Poland, Portugal and Spain.

So far, U2 has dropped the singles “Street of Dreams,” “The Greatest Show on Earth” and “Silencio” from their first full album of new material in nine years. The LP features the final vocal performance from late country icon Dolly Parton on the song “Torn,” which was co-written by the band, Parton and Snow Patrol’s Johnny McDaid, as well as a song dedicated to Rosalía titled “The Mirror Maker (Rosalía).

The band also recently announced a return to stadiums for their 2027 Carnaval De Luz Presents: The Greatest Show on Earth World Tour, which will kick off in Mexico City on Feb. 23 at Estadio GNP Seguros, followed by multiple nights in São Paulo, Brazil and Buenos Aires, Argentina and just announced shows in the U.K. and Europe.

entertainment.title: Gerry Cardinale’s RedBird Capital, Guy Oseary’s Sound Ventures Ink $1 Billion Investment Partnership
entertainment.summary: The Skydance and Artists Equity backer and the talent manager's investment firm will deploy the cash toward companies "at the convergence of technology, media and culture."
entertainment.body:
RedBird Capital Partners, the investment firm founded by Gerry Cardinale, and Sound Ventures, the investment company co-founded by music industry talent manager Guy Oseary , have inked a $1 billion dollar partnership.

The two firms will deploy that cash by investing in companies “at the convergence of technology, media and culture.”

It’s an area they know a thing or two about, given RedBird’s investments in companies like Skydance, Artists Equity and MARI, and Sound Ventures’ investments in company’s like Anthropic, OpenAI, Spotify and Uber.

RedBird will bring its global relationships and experience in business-building (it has specialists that help grow companies that they invest in) as well as its RedBird X AI team led by Hamid Biglari, while Sound Ventures will bring its extensive access to founders and its marketing skills.

Sound Ventures was founded by Oseary, whose music industry clients include Madonna, and actor Ashton Kutcher, with Kutcher leaving the firm earlier this year.

“The next great technology companies and the entrepreneur founders behind them need versatile partners who understand the long-term trajectory of company building and alpha generation,” Cardinale said in a statement. “Sound Ventures has established a strong track record built on founder relationships and high conviction plays in technology and AI, which includes early investments in both Anthropic and OpenAI. This partnership puts the power of RedBird’s institutional investment platform and strategic network firmly behind this next generation of business builders.”

“RedBird brings a different kind of outlook that complements what we have built at Sound, with the resources and scale to compound the impact of our investments,” added Oseary. “Effie [Epstein] and I are excited to work closely with Gerry, Hamid and the RedBird team as we continue to back exceptional founders and companies, building out this differentiated investment platform together.”

“Our two firms bring a shared ambition to invest at the forefront of innovation and support companies as they scale,” said Epstein. “RedBird is renowned for working closely with the businesses it backs, which mirrors our approach. Together we can help founders access the people, opportunities and resources that accelerate their ambitions.”

entertainment.title: TelevisaUnivision Quarterly U.S. Ad Revenue Falls 24 Percent, But World Cup Boosts Mexico Results
entertainment.summary: The Spanish-language media giant also posts record streaming revenue and a non-cash impairment loss of $372 million "related to the write-down of television broadcast licenses."
entertainment.body:
During the July-September quarter, rival NBCUniversal’s Telemundo featured the Spanish-language U.S. rights and games as part of the 2026 FIFA World Cup , which took place from late in the second to early in the third quarter. But World Cup momentum drove results across linear TV and streamer ViX in Mexico, where TelevisaUnivision had rights to the matches.

The U.S. ad results reflected “cyclical headwinds primarily from competitive sports programming and a prior-year comparison that included the Gold Cup,” the company said.

TelevisaUnivision also shared an update on its streaming business. The “DTC business delivered record revenue, with double-digit year-over[-year] growth, fueled by ViX’s performance during the quarter,” it said on Thursday.

“Our performance in the third quarter reflected disciplined execution against our multiplatform strategy as we delivered exceptional results from the World Cup in Mexico while gaining momentum in the U.S. with increased engagement across our fall content slate and robust sports portfolio,” said Daniel Alegre, CEO of TelevisaUnivision. “As we close out the year, we remain focused on maximizing the value of our content across multiple platforms to reach a wider audience and increase our monetization opportunities.”

Total company revenue in the third quarter grew 9 percent to $1.4 billion, driven by a 51 percent gain in Mexico, powered by the World Cup. TelevisaUnivision posted an operating loss of $119 million, a swing from an operating profit of $265 million. A non-cash impairment loss of $372 million “related to the write-down of television broadcast licenses” was the key reason. Adjusted operating income before depreciation and amortization (OIBDA) of $461 million was slightly down from $467 million in the year-ago period.

Total ad revenue in the third quarter declined 5 percent to $717 million, with the U.S. drop outweighing the growth in Mexico.

Total quarterly subscription and licensing revenue grew 30 percent to $640 million, driven by “approximately $90 million in revenue attributable to sublicensing the FIFA World Cup rights across Spanish-speaking Latin American countries and the expansion of ViX’s premium tier.” In the U.S., subscription and licensing revenue dropped 4 percent to $372 million “due to lower content licensing revenue, partially offset by pricing growth in ViX’s premium tiers,” the company said. In Mexico, the metric jumped 156 percent to $268 million, driven by content licensing and growth in ViX’s premium tier thanks to the World Cup. Operating expenses in the third quarter rose 14 percent to $918 million, or 11 percent when excluding foreign exchange impacts, hitting the bottom line. The change was “mainly driven by FIFA World Cup rights and production costs,” TelevisaUnivision said.

Logo text There’s no denying The Celebrity Traitors set a high bar.

Its first season aired in October last year and gave us some of the U.K.’s best reality TV in a long time: A traitorous Alan Carr murdering singer-songwriter Paloma Faith in plain sight, Celia Imrie farting in fear during a particularly spooky challenge, and the introduction of the “Big Dog” theory from sportsman Joe Marler, whose hypothesis — that producers would want at least one high-profile name in the turret — has, as we’ve come to find out, endured.

Some may argue that the second season, wrapping up on Friday, boasts an even starrier cast. Twenty-one famous faces were again invited to Ardross Castle in the Scottish Highlands, where three Traitors are tapped to secretly hunt, lie to, and ultimately murder the Faithful. In between the killings is a series of challenges where participants can contribute to a prize pot for their selected charity, as well as daily roundtables where the group can banish anyone they believe to be a Traitor.

entertainment.title: Cannes’ Marché du Film, TIFFCOM Commit to Second Edition of Japan IP Market in 2027
entertainment.summary: The event, running May 14–15 next year, is designed to help international producers navigate Japan’s complex rights landscape and develop adaptations of manga, novels and other IP.
entertainment.body:
TIFFCOM and the Marché du Film will hold a second Japan IP Market at the 2027 Cannes Film Festival, extending this year’s inaugural partnership, which was designed to connect Japanese rights holders with international producers and buyers.

The announcement was made Thursday during TIFFCOM in Tokyo, at the session “Beyond Country of Honour: Building the Next Global Partnerships with Japan.” Alexandra Zakharchenko, the Cannes market’s head of industry programs, was among the speakers.

The initiative is designed to facilitate adaptations, acquisitions and international collaborations involving Japanese intellectual property, giving overseas companies direct access to rights holders through pitches, targeted one-on-one meetings and industry discussions. Japan has long been viewed as a treasure trove of bankable manga, gaming and other forms of IP, but the country’s unique rights structures and ways of doing business have made collaboration more difficult for potential international partners. The TIFFCOM-Marché du Film partnership is designed to smooth that process. Related Stories Movies Janusz Kamiński to Receive THR Visionary in Cinematography Award Movies Black Nights Stars: What You Need to Know About the 10 Up-and-Comers in the Tallinn Spotlight

Its first edition launched in Cannes in May 2026 as part of Japan’s Country of Honor program at the Marché du Film. Participating companies included Kadokawa, Shochiku and Toei, while speakers included Tetsu Fujimura, founder and CEO of Filosophia and an executive producer of Netflix’s live-action One Piece .

The Cannes event is a counterpart to TIFFCOM’s Tokyo IP Market: Adaptation & Remake, which launched in 2025 and presents adaptation rights to manga and novels alongside film remake rights. Continuing the partnership gives Japanese companies opportunities to develop international relationships at both the Cannes gathering in May and the Tokyo market in October.

Organizers plan to announce the participating companies and further details of the 2027 program in the coming months.

entertainment.title: Janusz Kamiński to Receive THR Visionary in Cinematography Award
entertainment.summary: The two-time Oscar-winning cinematographer ('Schindler's List,' 'Saving Private Ryan') will be honored at the ToruńCamerimage Film Festival on Nov. 7.
entertainment.body:
Two-time Oscar-winning cinematographer Janusz Kamiński will receive this year’s THR Visionary in Cinematography Award at the ToruńCamerimage Film Festival .

The award recognizes Kamiński’s exceptional contribution to the art of cinematography and his visionary approach to shaping the visual language of modern filmmaking. He will receive the honor at the Toruń Camerimage festival on Nov. 7.

The acclaimed Polish filmmaker is among the most influential cinematographers in contemporary cinema. His work with Steven Spielberg — Kamiński has shot 20 films with Spielberg, including his latest, Disclosure Day — has rewritten the visual grammar of Hollywood. Related Stories Movies Black Nights Stars: What You Need to Know About the 10 Up-and-Comers in the Tallinn Spotlight Movies Cate Blanchett Warns Against "Unthinking Certainty" as She Accepts Japan's Praemium Imperiale

The stark black-and-white of Schindler’s List (1994) and the chaotic handheld battle scenes of Saving Private Ryan (1998), changed the look and feel or period drama and war films forever. Both won Kamiński the Oscar for Best Cinematography, and both were included in the American Society of Cinematographers’ list of the best-photographed films of the 20th century.

Every Kamiński film is beautiful, but not one of them looks the same. Every lens and every color choice matches the story being told. The tech-dystopian Washington of Minority Report (2002) is bleached in cold blues and metallic noir shadows. The style of Munich (2005) evokes the aesthetics of 1970s thrillers and news footage. In one of his non-Spielberg collaborations, Julian Schnabel’s The Diving Bell and the Butterfly (2007), Kamiński evokes the lead character’s locked-in syndrome with a radically restricted point of view and minute shifts in focus.

Kamiński’s life reads like a Hollywood movie. A political refugee from Poland, speaking no English when he arrived, he trained first at Columbia College in Chicago, then at the American Film Institute and rose through the ranks, working as a gaffer on no-budget Roger Corman productions and on TV movies. It was his work on Diane Keaton’s TV movie Wildflower (1991) that convinced Spielberg to offer him a job, first on the TV movie The Class of 61 , which Spielberg produced, then on Schindler’s List .

Kamiński has worked with the likes of Judd Apatow ( Funny People ) and Cameron Crowe ( Jerry Maguire ) but it is his work with Spielberg which has brought him the most acclaim, and 6 of his 7 Academy Award nominations for Best Cinematography.
