entertainment.title: Foo Fighters Pack a Punch For ‘Your Favorite Toy’ Performance on ‘Kimmel’: Watch
entertainment.summary: For their third trick on the late-night show’s Halloween takeover week, the Foos rocked out.
entertainment.body:
Even after 30 years of getting it done, the Foo Fighters can still rock the house. That house is typically a stadium, although this week the rockers scaled down and got back to their roots for a four-night musical residency on Jimmy Kimmel Live . Explore Foo Fighters See latest videos, charts and news

On night one, it was a performance of “Window” from the rock act’s 12th and latest studio album, Your Favorite Toy. Then, on Tuesday night, an old favorite with “This Is A Call,” lifted from the Foos’ debut self-titled album from 1995. Related Hayden Panettiere's Death Ruled as Accidental, Case Closed: Reports Forrest Frank Sets Release Date for New Album 'The Jesus Generation' J. Cole Reflects on Kendrick Lamar Feud & Confirms He's Not Retiring: 'I'm Not Using That Word at All'

For their third trick on the late-night show’s Halloween takeover week, another new number. Dave Grohl and Co. ripped through a performance of the title track from Your Favorite Toy, which unwrapped in April and debuted at No. 1 on Billboard ’s Top Hard Rock Albums chart, the Foos’ eighth leader .

The Foos got down to business for the type of loud, old school, no-fuss expression of rock that the band was built on. And they did it in a studio with a capacity they outgrew back in the mid-‘90s. A serious win for any fan who scored a pass.

Your Favorite Toy was “the most fun we’ve had making a record in years,” Grohl told Classic Rock ahead of its release. The Rock Hall-inducted group approached it with “no rules, no pressure — just the joy of plugging in and seeing what happens.”

The Foos’ world tour has this year taken the Rock Hall-inductees through North America, across Europe, and next week kicks off in Australia and New Zealand .

In a chat with Kimmel which aired earlier in the week, Grohl recounted how he poached Taylor Hawkins, his late drummer and friend, from Alanis Morissette; praised the music talents of his daughter Violet; and talked-up the band’s headline spot at KROQ’s Almost Acoustic Christmas event, set for Dec. 12 at the Kia Forum in Los Angeles.

The first time the Foos played the radio station’s fest was 1995, on a bill with Morissette, Porno For Pyros, Sonic Youth, Presidents of The United States of America, Garbage, No Doubt and Radiohead. “Those were the days,” Grohl remarked. “That was such a great time for music, you know. The ‘90s…everyone was young and excited and inspired and shows like that brought everyone together. It was really like a community.” The Foos’ latest late-night spot had that community spirit.

entertainment.body:
The international girl group’s Wildworld Tour expands with the addition of 11 new shows across Asia, Australia and New Zealand early next year.

Promoted by Live Nation , the new leg will get underway Jan. 27 at Yokohama Arena in Yokohama, Japan, then heads to Manila, Hong Kong, Seoul, Cebu, Singapore, Bangkok and Taipei. Following a 10-day break, the group returns to Australia for concerts in Sydney and Melbourne before wrapping things up March 5 at Auckland’s Spark Arena.

KATSEYE are making good on their promise of a prompt return to Australia . The two-time Grammy Award-nominated pop act made a whistlestop trip to these parts earlier in the year, where the singers participated in an exclusive fan Q&A experience and an industry showcase in Sydney, then performed for superfans in Melbourne. Bandmate Lara Raj went on to tell Australia’s Nova network “we love it here,” and “it would make us very happy to come back and spend a lot of time here.” Explore KATSEYE See latest videos, charts and news

entertainment.summary: The West Australian composers were honored for their work on the Australian Broadcasting Corporation’s animated kid’s series "Tales from Outer Suburbia."
entertainment.body:
With four victories, Josh Hogan and Ned Beckley were the big winners Wednesday night (Oct. 28) at the 2026 Screen Music Awards , presented at Brisbane’s Fortitude Music Hall. Explore Billboard See latest videos, charts and news

The West Australian composers were honored for their output on the Australian Broadcasting Corporation’s animated kid’s series Tales from Outer Suburbia , taking home best music for children’s programming, best opening title television theme and best soundtrack album, as well as best original song composed for the screen alongside composer Joni Hogan. Related Hayden Panettiere's Death Ruled as Accidental, Case Closed: Reports Forrest Frank Sets Release Date for New Album 'The Jesus Generation' J. Cole Reflects on Kendrick Lamar Feud & Confirms He's Not Retiring: 'I'm Not Using That Word at All'

It was a perfect night for the pair, as they snagged all four categories they were nominated for.

There were multiple donut-shaped awards, too, for Adam Gock and Dinesh Wicks, who bagged most performed screen composer – Australia for the 12th time for their work on MasterChef, My Kitchen Rules and Travel Guides ; plus most performed screen composer – overseas for Con Girl, Lego Masters and Married at First Sight ; and best music for unscripted or reality television series for Million Dollar Secret alongside fellow composers Adam Sofo, Brontë Horder, Cassie To, David Bruggemann, Lydia Davies, Mitch Stewart and Rory Chenoweth.

Helena Czajka went back-to-back in the best music for a documentary category, winning for Sentient , while Finn Clarke scooped emerging screen composer of the year. Benjamin Lam, Nicholas Gardiner, Georgina Darvidis, Matthew Sheers and Peter Corrigan were among the first-time winners.

As previously reported , Cezary Skubiszewski was feted with the distinguished services to the Australian screen award, in recognition of his impressive body of work spanning more than 30 years. Following a standing ovation, the prolific Polish music man was presented with the award by film producer Nelson Woss, with whom he collaborated on the soundtrack for Red Dog .

An initiative of APRA AMCOS (APRA this year celebrates its 100th anniversary) and the Australian Guild of Screen Composers (AGSC), the annual event celebrates excellence and innovation in screen composition across 16 categories, praising outstanding contributions in short film, television series, documentaries, children’s programming, feature films and more.

entertainment.title: Zach Bryan’s ‘Young Manhood and Other Donatable Organs’ Debuts Atop Three Album Charts
entertainment.summary: Plus, all eight of its tracks enter Hot Country Songs and Hot Rock Songs.
entertainment.body:
Zach Bryan ’s Young Manhood and Other Donatable Organs debuts at No. 1 on Billboard ’s Top Country Albums, Top Rock Albums and Americana/ Folk Albums charts , and No. 2 on the Billboard 200, earning 65,000 equivalent album units in the United States in its first week, Oct. 16-22, according to Luminate.

The set is Bryan’s fifth to top those three tallies. It follows January’s With Heaven on Top , 2024’s The Great American Bar Scene , 2023’s self-titled release and 2022’s American Heartbreak . With Heaven on Top and Zach Bryan also led the all-genre Billboard 200.

Young Manhood and Other Donatable Organs likewise makes an immediate splash at the song level. All eight of its tracks debut on Hot Country Songs and Hot Rock Songs, led by the Lana Del Rey-featuring “Lies,” which enters at No. 1 on the latter, becoming their fourth and first leader, respectively, and No. 2 on the former. The haul swells one of the deepest catalogs in the style, as Bryan has now charted 106 titles on Hot Rock Songs and 97 on Hot Country Songs.

Few artists open in the Hot Country Songs top 10 like Bryan. With “Lies” and “Lodi When” bowing at Nos. 2 and 9, he has now debuted 14 of his 17 career top 10s directly in the tier. That’s the third-most top 10 debuts among all acts since the chart adopted its multimetric methodology in October 2012, trailing only Morgan Wallen (34) and Taylor Swift (17). Bryan’s two No. 1s are “Something in the Orange” and his Kacey Musgraves collaboration “I Remember Everything,” which ruled for six and 20 weeks, respectively.

On the Billboard Hot 100, “Lies” enters at No. 4, becoming Bryan’s fourth top 10 and Del Rey’s third.

The streaming numbers also put Bryan’s reach in perspective. During the tracking week, he ranked fourth among all artists in the U.S., drawing 151.3 million official streams. He trailed only Drake (298.6 million), Wallen (204.2 million) and Swift (183.1 million).

entertainment.title: Hayden Panettiere’s Death Ruled as Accidental, Case Closed: Reports
entertainment.summary: The Greenville Police Department has confirmed that Panettiere's passing was not being treated as suspicious.
entertainment.body:
The investigation into Hayden Panettiere’ s death is now closed after an investigation found that an accidental overdose was to blame.

The Greenville Police Department has confirmed to reporters that the actor’s passing on Aug. 16 was not being treated as suspicious.

“Based on the Medical Examiner’s determination and the findings of the investigation, Hayden Panettiere’s death has been ruled accidental,” reads a statement provided to Entertainment Weekly . “The Greenville Police Department has concluded its investigation.”

That decision follows a coroner’s report, seen last month by Associated Press, that claimed her death was from an accidental overdose of several drugs, including fentanyl, following a stint in rehab. Explore Hayden Panettiere See latest videos, charts and news

The former Nashville and Heroes star was found in cardiac arrest at a residence in South Carolina, aged 36. “It is with profound sadness that we share the tragic passing of our beloved Hayden. She was an incredible light and a force of nature who brought immeasurable love and joy to all who knew her — and to the millions who watched her onscreen,” said her father, Skip Panettiere, in a statement. Panettiere had an 11-year-old daughter, Kaya Evdokia Klitschko, with ex-fiancé Wladimir Klitschko, the former heavyweight champion boxer. In 2018, she agreed to give full custody of Kaya to Klitschko amid her struggles with postpartum depression and addiction.

According to AP , it’s remains unclear whether federal authorities will separately continue to examine the case. In a petition last month to a California court, Klitschko noted that federal law enforcement agents had taken some of her items for their own probe. The U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration did not immediately respond to emailed requests from the news agency.

Though she was best known for her small screen work, which got underway with a commercial shoot at 11 months old for a Playskool toy train, back in 1990, Panettiere also left behind a music imprint thanks to her run on Nashville from 2012-2018.

entertainment.title: How Singapore’s F1 Grand Prix Became The ‘Coachella of Asia’
entertainment.summary: "No other festival in Asia possesses comparable buying power or influence" as the Singapore GP, WME's Brett Murrihy says.
entertainment.body:
SINGAPORE — With its combination of speed, glamor, artistry and science, Formula 1 is a spectacle that travels at a speed and sound nothing else can match.

It was Red Bull’s Max Verstappen who bagged the 2026 Formula 1 Singapore Airlines Singapore Grand Prix earlier this month with a pole-to-checkered flag win, an historic deed for the flying Dutchman who finally conquered a race that had eluded him for a decade . Related Kenny MacPherson, Veteran Music Publisher and Big Deal Music Co-Founder, Dies at 71 Jessica Lynch

If Verstappen was the king of the track, The Killers, Janet Jackson, Split Enz, JJ Lin and Lana Del Rey were the stars of the live show, a music festival that pumps away when the racing pauses.

With its flashy street circuit and three-day live music festival, the Singapore GP has a speed and sound quite unlike any other race on the calendar. Established in 2008, senior music industry executives are now calling it the premier annual music festival in Asia.

Billboard was there to catch the action Oct. 9-11, both on track and across the event’s 11 live entertainment stages.

Concert promoters pray for sunshine. The team behind the Singapore GP’s music festival did just that, and their prayers were mostly answered.

Slippery conditions for a Formula One Grand Prix aren’t just a bummer, they can be downright dangerous. When these rockets on wheels fly around bends and top speeds of 230 mph on the straight, grip is paramount.

Neil Finn performed with Crowded House at the Singapore F1 GP last year, and returned this time with the reunited art-rock legends Split Enz. Finn always brings the weather with him, not a talent that’s ideal for these circumstances. So, for the Enz’ opening night set at the Wharf stage, in Zone 1, the New Zealand songsmith sent out a message of good luck “to all the drivers and all the teams. Let’s hope they go real fast. And stay real safe.”
